title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay in expectations; value is what the asset base actually earns once acquisition goodwill, tariffs, and regulatory friction are accounted for.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Principle

web_blocks.html: At the 2026-11-25 live TradingView close of ₹1,843.00 (2026-11-23 NSE ledger ₹1,796.50), Screener market cap is ₹1,06,013 crore (₹1,03,395.4 Cr on TV) [1][23]. Shares trade at 26.1x Screener TTM P/E (26.72x TV), 2.69x book value (₹685), and a 0.38% dividend yield [1][23]. After rallying +54.61% over 12 months from ₹1,106.00 to near its ₹1,859.90 high, deep-value pricing is gone [23]. Yet it still trades at a 10%–38% discount to large-cap peers. That discount reflects 12.9% ROCE (10.1% ROE), four USFDA OAI/WL formulation sites, and Pen-G's Jan 2027 MIP cliff [1][8][9][32][34].

web_blocks.caption: Indian Large-Cap Pharmaceutical Peer Valuation & Quality Comparison (2026-11-25 Live TradingView Snapshot)
web_blocks.takeaway: Source Reconciliation: TradingView TTM P/E and ROE print 26.72x/10.72% (AUROPHARMA), 41.59x/13.13% (SUNPHARMA), 40.00x/8.48% (CIPLA), 41.65x/7.52% (DRREDDY), 17.64x/23.84% (LUPIN), and 29.69x/15.74% (ZYDUSLIFE), while Screener.in consolidated P/E and ROCE print 26.1x/12.9%, 37.0x/20.5%, 37.2x/15.5%, 41.8x/13.0%, 16.2x/29.9%, and 27.3x/21.1% [1][23][24][25][26][27][38]. Across both feeds, Aurobindo trades at a discount to specialty/branded peers because its 12.9% ROCE and four-site USFDA formulation backlog cap its multiple [1][8][9][32].

web_blocks.html: A ten-year check confirms 26.1x P/E sits in the upper half of Aurobindo's historical band [1]. In its FY15–FY18 peak-ROCE era (23%–27%), shares traded at 18x–24x forward earnings [1]. In the FY22–FY23 trough (9%–10% ROCE), multiples fell to 11x–15x [1]. Today's price equals roughly 15.0x EV/EBITDA on a ₹1,03,011 crore enterprise value against ₹6,870 crore FY26 EBITDA [1][2]. The market already credits Q2 FY27's ₹10,263 crore run-rate, including inorganic sales from the June 29, 2026 $245.7M Lannett deal [3][33].

web_blocks.takeaway: A Reverse DCF at ₹1,843.00 proves the market prices in ~11% 10-year revenue growth, 21% EBITDA margins, and a 400–500 bps ROCE recovery—leaving virtually no margin of safety against four USFDA formulation OAI/WL sites, the Jan 2027 Pen-G MIP cliff, and unresolved MDL 2724 antitrust exposure [1][23][32][34][36].

web_blocks.title: FY28E Normalized EPS & Risk-Adjusted Fair Value Anchor
web_blocks.the_number: ₹78.70 FY28E Base EPS (₹94.00 Bull; ₹72.00 Bear); Base Fair Value ₹1,850.00 at 23.5x FY28E EPS
web_blocks.how_calculated: ₹8,750 Cr EBITDA + ₹450 Cr other income − ₹2,200 Cr D&A (reflecting post-Lannett & CWIP depreciation) − ₹430 Cr interest = ₹6,570 Cr PBT; at audited 31% tax = ₹4,533 Cr PAT / 57.6 Cr shares = ₹78.70 EPS.
web_blocks.the_inputs: FY26 PAT ₹3,503 Cr (31.5% audited tax); Europe >€1B (+27% YoY in Q2 FY27); Lannett revenue offset by Seymour OAI remediation; Pen-G 10,000 MTPA assuming DGTR relief; net cash ₹3,002 Cr [1][2][3][32][33][34].
web_blocks.if_off: If any of the four OAI/WL formulation sites escalates to an Import Alert, Pen-G MIP lapses without timely DGTR duties, or MDL 2724 triggers a large cash settlement, FY28E EPS falls toward ₹72.00 and P/E compresses to 18x (₹1,296.00).

web_blocks.title: Why Peer Discounts Persist—And Why Zydus & Lupin Set a Higher Bar
paragraphs: At 26.1x Screener P/E (26.72x TV), Aurobindo looks cheaper than Sun Pharma (37.0x), Cipla (37.2x), and Dr. Reddy's (41.8x) [1][24][25][26]. Yet Sun earns 20.5% ROCE with patented US drugs. Zydus trades at 27.3x Screener P/E with 21.1% ROCE and fresh Nov 25 USFDA EIRs [24][38].

Lupin trades at just 16.2x Screener P/E (17.64x TV) with 29.9% ROCE and 28.7% ROE, though it sits below its 200D SMA (₹2,229.20) [27]. Aurobindo will not re-rate past 26x until ROCE clears 16% and its four FDA backlogs clear.

web_blocks.html: Sum-of-the-Parts & Risk-Adjusted Asymmetry: Core US/Europe generics and Apitoria APIs (backed by Nov VAI EIRs) warrant 18x–20x earnings [31][32]. Upon FDA clearance and CDMO scaling, Eugia and CuraTeQ/TheraNym merit 25x–28x [11][17]. Blending to 23.5x on FY28E Base EPS of ₹78.70 yields ₹1,850.00. At live TV CMP ₹1,843.00, upside is +0.38% against -13.22% stop risk to ₹1,599.40 (0.03:1 R/R). Even at our ₹1,718.52–₹1,750.00 support band, R/R is just 0.66:1 at ₹1,750.00 (1.10:1 at ₹1,718.52)—failing 1.50:1 [23]. MDL 2724 legal risk and ₹460.27 Cr Lannett goodwill reinforce that cap [33][36].

Valuation Decision Trigger: Neither live TV CMP ₹1,843.00 (0.03:1 R/R) nor ₹1,718.52–₹1,750.00 support (0.66:1 at top) clears 1.50:1 against ₹1,850.00 fair value. New capital is REJECTED on valuation [23]. VAI clearances across Eugia/Seymour plus DGTR Pen-G duties lift value toward ₹2,350.00 [8][9][32][34]. An Import Alert or close below ₹1,599.40 exits held shares [23].

book_paragraphs: Now that our Pass 1 forensic refresh has audited every new filing through November 25, 2026—including Apitoria Pharma's clean Unit-VI VAI clearance, the $245.7 million Lannett acquisition and its Seymour OAI, Kakinada Pen-G's January 2027 policy cliff, US Section 232 tariff risks, and Aurobindo's unresolved MDL 2724 antitrust exposure—let's open the valuation tape and ask the defining question: why does the market price this business at ₹1,843.00 today?

Let's keep our two market timestamps strictly separate so there is zero confusion. On the official November 23, 2026 NSE session ledger, Aurobindo closed at ₹1,796.50. Two days later, on the November 25, 2026 live TradingView snapshot, the stock rallied +2.59% to ₹1,843.00—just 0.91% below its 52-week high of ₹1,859.90 and up +54.61% over the past twelve months from its ₹1,106.00 low. At ₹1,843.00, Screener.in puts market capitalization at ₹1,06,013 crore (TradingView reports ₹1,03,395.4 crore on slightly different diluted share counts), translating to 26.1 times Screener trailing earnings, 26.72 times TradingView TTM P/E, 2.69 times ₹685 book value, and a 0.38% dividend yield.

Subtract Aurobindo's ₹3,002 crore in net cash from its ₹1,06,013 crore market cap and you get an enterprise value of roughly ₹1,03,011 crore, or about 15.0 times FY26 operating EBITDA of ₹6,870 crore. That immediately tells us one vital truth: the easy deep-value phase—when investors could buy Aurobindo at 11 to 15 times depressed FY22–FY23 earnings—is completely behind us. Today's multiple sits squarely in the upper half of Aurobindo's ten-year trading range, even higher than the 18-to-24-times forward multiple it commanded back in FY15–FY18 when its return on capital employed was 23% to 27%.

Yet look across the Indian large-cap pharmaceutical peer table and you still see a wide valuation gap. On Screener.in as of November 25, Sun Pharma trades at 37.0 times earnings (41.59x on TradingView), Cipla trades at 37.2 times (40.00x TV), Dr. Reddy's trades at 41.8 times (41.65x TV), and Zydus Lifesciences trades at 27.3 times (29.69x TV). Why does Aurobindo trade at a 10% to 38% discount to those large-cap peers?

The answer sits squarely in capital efficiency and regulatory friction. Sun Pharma earns a 20.5% ROCE backed by a patented US specialty franchise. Zydus Lifesciences earns a 21.1% ROCE and just cleared USFDA EIRs at SEZ II and Ankleshwar on November 25. Aurobindo, by contrast, earns a 12.9% ROCE and a 10.1% ROE because ₹24,902 crore of gross fixed assets and capital work-in-progress—recently swollen by ₹1,861.57 crore of provisional net assets and ₹460.27 crore of goodwill from the June 29, 2026 Lannett acquisition—are still ramping up alongside 326 days of inventory. Worse, instead of just two sterile plants under USFDA pressure, our Pass 1 audit confirmed four formulation sites in OAI or Warning Letter status: Eugia Unit III, Eugia Unit II Bhiwadi, Eugia Unit I, and Lannett's Seymour, Indiana facility.

Let's run a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow test at ₹1,843.00 to see what future the market is already pricing in. Using an 11.5% cost of capital and a 4.5% terminal growth rate, an enterprise value of ₹1,03,011 crore requires Aurobindo to compound consolidated revenue at roughly 10.8% to 11.4% annually for the next decade while sustaining 20.5% to 21.5% EBITDA margins, pulling capex-to-sales down toward 6.5%–7.5% after TheraNym Unit 2 is built, and lifting incremental ROIC from 12.9% back to 16%–18% by FY29.

Pause and weigh how demanding that implied expectation really is. Over the past five years, Aurobindo's actual sales CAGR was 6.32%. While Q2 FY27 jumped +23.9% YoY to a record ₹10,263 crore—with Europe surging +27% YoY to ₹3,161 crore (€288 million) and US formulations rising +25% YoY to ₹4,555 crore—Pass 1 proved that the US jump was not purely organic. It included inorganic contribution from the $245.7 million Lannett acquisition, which also brought ₹40.18 crore in exceptional transaction costs and an immediate November 11 USFDA OAI at Seymour, Indiana.

Then examine the margin assumption baked into ₹1,843.00. Sustaining 21% consolidated EBITDA margins assumes Kakinada Penicillin-G remains solidly profitable as gRevlimid exclusivity fades. Yet Pass 1 uncovered that Kakinada's EBITDA turnaround leaned heavily on India's January 29, 2026 DGFT Minimum Import Price floor—₹2,216/kg on Pen-G, ₹2,733/kg on Amoxicillin, and ₹3,405/kg on 6-APA—which expires in January 2027. That is why subsidiary Lyfius Pharma petitioned India's DGTR to open anti-dumping investigation AD/OI/057/2026 against Chinese Pen-G imports on September 28, 2026. If anti-dumping duties are delayed or set below the MIP floor, Pen-G margins could compress right when depreciation peaks.

Add two more unpriced tail risks from Pass 1. First, US Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs: while generics received a temporary exemption on April 2, 2026, they remain under a one-year Commerce Department review alongside a July 21, 2026 presidential warning of 100% generic tariffs by August 2028 absent domestic US manufacturing—making Seymour's OAI remediation strategically urgent rather than optional. Second, Aurobindo Pharma USA remains a non-settling defendant in the multistate US generic price-fixing antitrust litigation (MDL No. 2724), where peers settled heavily in 2026: Sandoz for $400 million in October, Glenmark for $29.6 million in November, and Lannett/Bausch for $17.85 million in February with cooperation obligations.

Now let's translate all of those verified positives and negatives into disciplined FY28E normalized earnings. We credit Europe's €1 billion+ engine (+27% YoY), Apitoria's clean November USFDA VAI clearances at Unit-II and Unit-VI, CuraTeQ's EMA approvals with STADA, and Pen-G scaling toward 10,000 metric tonnes assuming DGTR relief. Against that, we model higher post-Lannett and CWIP depreciation (₹2,200 crore vs ₹2,150 crore prior), ₹430 crore in interest, and modest Seymour remediation drag. That gives ₹8,750 crore FY28E EBITDA plus ₹450 crore other income minus ₹2,200 crore depreciation and ₹430 crore interest, equaling ₹6,570 crore in pre-tax profit. Applying Aurobindo's audited 31% effective tax rate yields ₹4,533 crore in net profit, or ₹78.70 per share across 57.6 crore shares.

Applying a blended 23.5-times sum-of-the-parts multiple—18x–20x for core US/Europe oral generics and Apitoria APIs, blended with 25x–28x optionality for Eugia injectables, CuraTeQ biosimilars, and TheraNym CDMO—puts our base-case fair value at ₹1,849.45, or ₹1,850.00 per share. Notice how trim that is: at ₹1,843.00 live TradingView CMP, base-case upside is just +0.38% against -13.22% downside to our ratcheted ₹1,599.40 structural stop—a 0.03-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. Even if the stock pulls back to our ₹1,718.52–₹1,750.00 support zone near the 10-week EMA (₹1,744.69) and Pivot R1 (₹1,748.37), upside from ₹1,750.00 to ₹1,850.00 is +5.71% against -8.61% stop risk—just 0.66-to-1 R/R, and only 1.10-to-1 even at the ₹1,718.52 lower edge.

Compare that against your other Indian pharma benchmarks. Lupin trades at 16.2 times Screener earnings (17.64x TradingView) with 29.9% ROCE and 28.7% ROE—nearly double Aurobindo's capital efficiency at a 38% cheaper multiple, even though Lupin's chart is still repairing below its 200-day moving average. Zydus Lifesciences trades at 27.3 times Screener earnings with 21.1% ROCE and clean November 25 FDA clearances, offering 2.03-to-1 asymmetry on a pullback into its support band.

In our bull case—where Eugia and Seymour clear their FDA overhangs, DGTR locks in Pen-G protection, and CuraTeQ scales—FY28E EPS can reach ₹94.00 at 25 times earnings, or ₹2,350.00. In our bear case—where an Import Alert strikes, Pen-G MIP lapses without timely relief, or MDL 2724 hits cash—depressed FY28E EPS of ₹72.00 at 18 times points to ₹1,296.00. With base fair value at ₹1,850.00 failing our 1.50-to-1 hurdle both at CMP and at support, valuation firmly rejects new capital today.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: At ₹1,843.00 (26.1x Screener P/E; 26.72x TV), the market already prices in smooth ~11% revenue compounding and 21% margins. Factoring in post-Lannett depreciation, four OAI/WL formulation sites, the Jan 2027 Pen-G MIP cliff, and MDL 2724 tail risk trims FY28E Base EPS to ₹78.70 and Base Fair Value to ₹1,850.00—leaving 0.03:1 R/R at CMP and 0.66:1 at support.
